paper.title: No-Regret Learning from Partially Observed Data in Repeated Auctions

settings.name_in_paper: Repeated auction with partially observed data (losing bidders observe a set of losing actions)
unmapped: Side observations only when the chosen action is a losing (zero-allocation) bid: the learner then observes a subset L_t of actions sharing the same loss l(0)
The learner is assumed to know the revelation probabilities r_t[k] of observing each action's loss
The learner knows the average feedback information alpha_avg (used to tune eta)
Losses arise from a repeated auction against other (possibly learning) bidders
settings.definition_quote: At every round $t$ bidder~$\ell$ picks an action $k(t) \in  \mathcal{K}_\ell$, an adversarial environment selects a \emph{loss vector} $\mathbf{l}_t \in [0,\,1]^{|\mathcal{K}_\ell|}$, and bidder~$\ell$ incurs loss $\mathbf{l}_t[k(t)]$. ... assume bidder~$\ell$ loses the auction ... bidder~$\ell$ gets to know of a subset $\mathcal{L}_t\subseteq\mathcal{K}_\ell$ of losing actions

algorithms.name: Extended Exp3 (MWU with revelation-probability importance-weighted estimator)

symbols.alpha_avg: average feedback information: inverse of the average over t and k of w_t[k]/r_t[k], in [1,K]

conditions: revelation probabilities r_t[k] are known to the learner (estimator unbiased)

source.label: thm:main
source.quote: Assume bidder~$\ell$ bids according to Algorithm~\ref{alg:MWU} with loss vector estimate $\tilde{\mathbf{l}}_t$ computed as in \eqref{eq:our_estimator} and $\eta = \sqrt{2 \alpha_\text{avg} \log(K) /(K T)}$, then $$ \mathbb{E} \big[ R_\ell(T) \big]\leq \sqrt{2\;(K/\alpha_\text{avg}) T \log K} \,. $$

results.notes: Regret defined with max over k inside expectation (expected_regret), though the proof effectively treats losses as fixed. Tuning requires alpha_avg, which is only computable after all rounds. Mapping to graph_feedback is approximate; environment kept unspecified.

cited_results.setting_description: Adversarial experts, full information, K actions, losses in [0,1]
Adversarial bandits with feedback graphs revealed after action

bound.regime: m_t upper bound on max acyclic subgraph size at round t; Sum_m_t = sum_t m_t
